rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting software that sets rents using nonpublic competitor data (such as real-time rents, lease renewals and occupancy levels) for residential rental property in Santa Ana. Tenants only need to prove the landlord used the prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits; applies to sellers, licensors, providers and users of covered rent-setting software.
rules.exemptions: Pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data or aggregate historical data, and tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the software uses nonpublic competitor data; landlord's use of such software cannot be determined from property data.

rules.penalty: Affected tenant may sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting ordinance (first reading Feb. 17, 2026; municipal code citation not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
rules.conflict_note: Source (dated Feb. 24, 2026) reports only first-reading approval on Feb. 17, 2026 with final vote set for March 3, 2026. Final adoption and effective date are not confirmed by this document; if adopted March 3, a California city ordinance would typically take effect ~30 days later (early April 2026) and would be in force by 2026-10-01.
